Tour Dekho is a travel marketplace where travellers compare whole packages from verified local agencies, customise the trip with a live estimate, and book with confidence.

a story about planning one more trip ✈

Every local agency leaving your city, compared in one place.

3 products

Website · App · Agency workspace — one design system

the idea

Compare · Customise · Confirm

01

Planning a trip in India still means twelve tabs, six phone calls and four PDFs that can’t be compared.

Most Indian holidays are sold by small local agencies. They know their routes best, but travellers can’t find them, compare them, or trust them — and the agencies can’t reach the travellers.

3–5 lakh

Travel agents estimated in India — only about 14,221 are registered with the Ministry of Tourism or trade bodies.

Source: TTG Asia

80–85%

Of the holiday-package market was serviced by individual agents — an opaque market for travellers.

Source: Business Today (2016), quoting TravelTriangle

86% → 40%

Of internet users are influenced online while researching, yet around 40% still book offline — mainly because they don’t trust online payments and terms.

Source: Bain & Company × Google, “How Does India Travel”

These numbers point to one gap: discovery and trust. Demand is online, supply is offline, and nothing in between lets people compare like for like.

“One more trip” — Ananya plans Manali with friends

A composite scenario built from secondary research — Ananya and Rohit are not real people, but every step reflects a documented pain point. Illustrations generated with Figma AI.

1 · “Let’s go to Manali!”

Ananya (27, Bengaluru) and three friends lock a December long weekend. Everyone has a budget; nobody has a plan.

2 · Twelve tabs later

Every agency site looks different and hides what’s actually included.

3 · The WhatsApp PDF pile

Six calls, four PDFs: 3★ vs 4★, sedan vs tempo, breakfast or not. Nothing compares like for like.

4 · “Can I upgrade the hotel?”

Every change = another call and a 24-hour wait for a new quote.

5 · “Is this agent even real?”

6 · Meanwhile, in Manali…

Rohit (Trailbound Travels) runs great trips but buys leads, lives in WhatsApp + Excel and can’t reach travellers in Bengaluru.

two sides of the same problem →

A 50% UPI advance to an agency with no reviews. The group chat goes quiet.

For travellers

“I can’t compare packages fairly, and I don’t know who to trust.”

Packages differ in hotel, car, sights and meals, so prices can’t be compared

For local agencies

Payouts and commissions are hard to track

Problem statement

Travellers in Indian cities need a trustworthy way to compare and customise complete trips from local agencies, because today every quote is different, slow to change and hard to trust. Local agencies need a simple way to reach those travellers without giving up control of their packages.

How might we…

…show packages from many agencies in one comparable format?

…let travellers change hotel, car, places and days and see the price update instantly?

…make a small, unknown agency feel as trustworthy as a big brand?

…give agencies a free tool simpler than WhatsApp + Excel?

What I set out to design

Challenge

Turn a fragmented, offline, low-trust market into one place where trips can be compared, customised and booked.

Goal

Design a two-sided marketplace: a traveller website + app, and a workspace for agencies to list and manage packages.

Primary users

Urban travellers aged 22–40 planning domestic trips from their city — solo, couples, friends and families.

Secondary users

Small and mid-size local travel agencies, homestays and cab fleets; group trip hosts.

Scope

Discovery → compare → customise → checkout → my trips; group departures; stays, tables & rides; agency onboarding, packages, bookings & payouts.

Constraints

INR pricing and GST; trust in payments; agencies with low tech comfort; mobile-first users; partner handoffs (OYO, Agoda, Booking.com…).

Success metrics (targets to validate)

A traveller compares 3 packages for the same route in under 5 minutes

At least 1 in 2 bookings uses a customisation (room, car, places or days)

Fees and inclusions understood before payment (no “surprise” fees in testing)

An agency lists its first package in under 10 minutes

Project brief

Search once. See every agency. Make it yours.

“Tour” is the trip; “Dekho” means “look / see” in Hindi. Tour Dekho lines up every verified local agency running your route — Bengaluru → Manali, Kolkata → Goa — with what’s really included, then lets you tweak the trip and watch the price update live.

…and this is how it should feel.

01

Compare

Packages from every agency on your route, in one format: stay, car, sights, meals, price.

02

Customise

Change room rating, car type, places and days. The estimate updates instantly — no re-quotes.

03

Confirm

Verified agencies, honest reviews, the full price breakdown before you pay.

04

For agencies

A free workspace to list packages, set upgrade prices, manage bookings and get paid in 48 h.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Compare whole packages, not just hotels or flights

OTAs already compare flights and hotels well. The unsolved job is comparing complete trips — so the core unit of Tour Dekho is the package, normalised into the same fields (stay, car, places, meals, days, price) for every agency.

02

A huge, growing market — sold through a long tail of small agencies no app has organised.

I used secondary research (industry reports, trade press, company disclosures) to size the opportunity, map competitors and frame who Tour Dekho is for.

How big is the opportunity?

₹16.8 tn

Domestic travel spending forecast in India for 2025 — the core of the market.

Source: WTTC via TravTalk India

$41.7 bn

India’s travel market in 2025, forecast to grow 13% to $47.2 bn in 2026.

Source: Phocuswright

57%

Online penetration of Indian travel in 2025 — offline still sells the rest.

Source: Phocuswright

2.95 bn

Domestic tourist visits recorded in India in 2024.

Source: Ken Research

What this means for Tour Dekho

Domestic trips are the backbone of Indian travel, and that is exactly where local agencies are strongest.

Almost half the market still books offline — the gap is trust and comparability, not demand.

Hotels and flights are already well served online; complete packages from small agencies are not.

Competitive analysis

Who travellers use today — and the gap they leave

I studied five alternatives: the biggest OTA, two holiday marketplaces, a DIY planner and the default — a local agent on WhatsApp.

MakeMyTrip Holidays

Largest Indian OTA — about 54% of online travel (Skift).

Does well

Trust, scale, payments, hotels & flights in one app.

Gap

Sells its own packages; small local agencies are invisible; little like-for-like comparison.

TravelTriangle

Holiday marketplace: 650+ agents send up to 3 quotes (Business Today, Preqin).

Does well

Proved that travellers want competing quotes from agents.

Gap

Quotes take 4–24 hours; every change is a new quote; agent brand is hidden.

Thrillophilia

10,000+ packages via 4,500 local partners (company figures).

Does well

Huge catalogue, strong reviews, group tours.

Gap

One brand in front; travellers can’t see or compare the agencies behind it.

Pickyourtrail

DIY builder for customisable international holidays.

Does well

Live, self-serve customisation with instant pricing.

Gap

Mostly international; one provider, no agency choice.

Local agent + WhatsApp

The default for millions of Indian travellers.

Does well

Personal, flexible, deep local knowledge.

Gap

Opaque prices, PDFs that can’t be compared, no reviews, risky advance payments.

Tour Dekho

Opportunity

Combine TravelTriangle’s many-agency choice with Pickyourtrail’s live customisation — for domestic trips, starting from the traveller’s own city — and give agencies their brand back.

the gap!

Positioning

The empty corner: many agencies + live customisation

Plotting alternatives by choice of provider and how freely you can shape the trip shows the gap. Marketplaces offer choice but slow re-quotes; DIY builders offer control but one provider. Tour Dekho sits where both meet.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Agencies set upgrade prices once — the app does the maths

To make live customisation possible across many agencies, each agency defines its upgrade options and prices (room rating, car type, places, extra day) in the workspace. Travellers then see instant estimates instead of waiting for re-quotes.

Want fixed-date group departures to travel with new people safely and cheaply.

Families

Local agencies & hosts

Why I designed it this way ✎

Start every search from the traveller’s own city

The journey shows people think “Bengaluru → Manali”, not just “Manali”. Search, results and packages are organised by departure-city route, which also lets agencies in departure cities compete with those at the destination.

03

Friendly, bold and honest — a marketplace that feels like a holiday, not a spreadsheet.

Comparing prices is serious work, so the visual language does the opposite: warm paper backgrounds, chunky ink outlines, sunny colour blocks and illustrated travellers. The reference was the playful, confident style of consumer apps like Chowdeck.

Honest by default

Every price shows what’s included and what’s extra. Fees appear before payment, never after.

Local first

Agencies keep their name, logo and reviews. The platform frames them; it doesn’t replace them.

Calm comparisons

One format for every package so differences are easy to spot — highlights, not walls of text.

Joyful, not noisy

Colour and illustration carry emotion; layouts stay simple, with one main action per screen.

Warm paper, sunny blocks, real destinations

Keywords: friendly · bold · local · sunny · trustworthy · Indian.

Logo blues for trust, sunshine for action

The two blues come straight from the logo. Navy carries trust (primary buttons, prices, headers); sun yellow marks the active choice; pastels colour-code categories.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Ink outlines instead of shadows

Thick 2px ink outlines keep cards readable on warm paper, print well in screenshots shared on WhatsApp, and give the brand a hand-made, friendly feel. Shadows are reserved for floating UI only.

Plus Jakarta Sans — one family, 11 sizes on an 8-pt rhythm

Sizes: 12 · 14 · 16 · 20 · 24 · 28 · 32 · 48 · 64 · 72 · 80. Labels use Title Case — never all caps.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Switched from Poppins to Plus Jakarta Sans

The first brand board used Poppins. Its geometric figures made long price tables feel wide and childish. Plus Jakarta Sans keeps the friendly round shapes but is more compact, has clearer numerals for ₹ prices, and has enough weights (Regular → ExtraBold) to build hierarchy with one family.

One component library for website, app and agency workspace

Colour and spacing are Figma variables; type is 20 text styles; components have variants and properties so every screen stays consistent.

Why I designed it this way ✎

One library, three products

Travellers move between website and app, and agencies use both sides. Sharing one set of tokens and components means a price, a badge or a button means the same thing everywhere — and changes ship to all three products at once.

04

A suitcase that’s already taking off.

From my earlier identity presentation: the name, the mark, the drafts and the iterations that led to the final logo.

The name

“Tour” is the trip — travel, stays, food, transport. “Dekho” is Hindi for “look / see / discover”. Together: go and look for your next tour — “Let’s have one more trip.”

The mark

A rolling suitcase whose body becomes a plane: packing and departing in one shape. Rounded corners and a slight tilt add motion and friendliness.

The tagline

Plan · Explore · Repeat — the loop every traveller goes through, and the reason to come back to the app.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Kept the logo blue, built the UI palette around it

I explored red, orange, green and black versions of the mark. I chose blue because it reads as calm and dependable for a product that handles payments, so the logo blues became the primary UI colours and the warm accents (sun, coral, pink) were added around them for the holiday feeling.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Route-first navigation

Search, results and package cards always show “From → To · dates”. It matches how people talk about trips and lets departure-city agencies compete fairly.

Why I designed it this way ✎

One door, two roles

Travellers and agencies use the same brand and the same sign-in entry, then split by role. On the website the “For agencies” link in the top nav leads to the same agency journey.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Different tab bars for different jobs

Travellers get Explore · Saved · Trips · Inbox · You. Agencies get Dashboard · Packages · Bookings · Payouts · More — mirroring the website sidebar so agencies can switch devices without relearning.

Customise: live estimate

v1 spread choices across long lists. v2 uses compact option cards, a stepper for days and a sticky price bar that updates instantly.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Greyscale before colour

Starting without colour forced every screen to work on hierarchy alone. It made reviews faster — feedback was about content and flow, not taste — and became the base for the 8-pt grid used in hi-fi.

07

The final screens.

Every screen is built from the shared library — 8-pt spacing, one type family, the same buttons, chips and cards on web and app.

Why I designed it this way ✎

Fixed navigation, scrolling content

The website’s top navigation and the app’s tab bar stay fixed while content scrolls, so search, trips and account are always one tap away — important on long results and comparison pages.

For agencies — on the website and in the app

How I’ll test it — and what I already fixed.

Usability tests with real travellers and agencies are the next step. Below is the test plan with space for results, followed by an expert (heuristic) review I ran on my own designs. No results here are invented.

Goal

Can travellers compare, customise and book a trip without help? Can agencies list a package and handle a booking?

Participants

5 travellers (22–40, planned a domestic trip in the last 12 months) + 5 owners or staff of small travel agencies.

Method

Moderated, think-aloud sessions on the Figma prototype, 30–40 min each, in person or remote.

Metrics

Task success, time on task, errors, ease rating per task (SEQ, 1–7), System Usability Scale (target ≥ 75).

Heuristic review of my own designs — issues found and fixed

Run against Nielsen’s 10 usability heuristics while designing. These are design-side fixes, not user-test findings.

Issue found

Heuristic

Fix

Labels in ALL CAPS were harder to scan and inconsistent across products

Consistency & standards

All labels changed to Title Case; a single “Eyebrow 12” style replaces uppercase overlines

Content slid under the tab bar and navigation disappeared on long pages

Visibility of system status

Screens now scroll with a fixed top nav (web) and fixed tab bar & sticky price bars (app)

Agencies shown only as initials didn’t build trust

Recognition rather than recall

Every agency avatar now shows its logo, alongside verified badge and rating

Button heights drifted (56 vs 60 px) and some text used off-scale sizes (15, 22, 26, 40)

Aesthetic & minimalist design

Buttons locked to 56 / 48 / 40; all text snapped to the 11-size scale

Agencies had no mobile path and travellers had no way to the agency side in the app

Flexibility & efficiency

Role-based sign-in plus a full mobile agency workspace mirroring the web sidebar

Fees could surprise travellers at the last step

Error prevention

Price summary shows package, upgrades, platform fee and GST before payment

Turning a design into a business.

How Tour Dekho could make money, how big the opportunity is, and — the hardest part of any marketplace — how to bring travel agents on board.

₹16.8 tn

Domestic travel spending in India, 2025 forecast — the total pool

Source: WTTC via TravTalk India

3–5 lakh

Travel agents in India — the supply Tour Dekho can organise

Source: TTG Asia

5–10%

Commission range proven by India’s holiday marketplaces

Source: Business Today; StartupTalky

Seven ways Tour Dekho earns — most only when an agency earns

Core

Booking commission

8–12% of the package value, charged to the agency only when a trip is booked (shown in the agency Payouts screen).

Core

Platform fee

A small, visible fee per booking paid by the traveller (₹600 in the checkout design).

Growth

Featured placement

Agencies pay to boost packages on busy routes or seasons, clearly labelled as promoted.

Growth

Agency Pro

Subscription for CRM, WhatsApp integration, team seats and demand insights.

Add-on

Partner commissions

Affiliate revenue from stays, restaurants and cabs handed off to partners.

Add-on

Insurance & add-ons

Travel insurance, activity add-ons and airport transfers at checkout.

Add-on

Group trip hosts

Fee from hosts and creators who run fixed-date departures on the platform.

Value for agencies

Why a travel agent would say yes

No listing fee — pay only when a booking happens

Reach travellers in other cities, not just walk-ins and referrals

A free workspace that replaces WhatsApp + Excel for quotes and bookings

Keep their own brand, logo and reviews

Upgrade prices set once, so no more re-typing quotes

Payout 48 hours after the trip starts, with clear commission statements

Demand alerts: which routes and dates travellers are searching

How to go to travel agents — supply first, one city at a time

Marketplaces fail when travellers arrive to empty shelves, so agencies come first.

Phase 0

Validate

Interview 20 agencies in Bengaluru and Manali and 20 travellers. Test the prototype; confirm commission tolerance and pain points.

Phase 1

Seed supply

Hand-onboard 50–100 agencies on 5 popular routes from one city. Field visits, trade bodies (TAAI, ADTOI, OTOAI, IATO), trade fairs (SATTE, OTM) and agency WhatsApp groups. “We’ll build your first package with you in 10 minutes.”

Phase 2

Bring travellers

Route landing pages for search (“Bengaluru to Manali package”), Instagram travel creators, referrals, and group-trip hosts who bring their audience.

Phase 3

Expand & deepen

Add departure cities, launch Agency Pro, partner integrations (stays, cabs) and insurance.

Founding-partner offer

Lower commission for the first 6 months, a verified badge from day one and priority placement on launch routes — in exchange for listing at least 3 packages and responding within 2 hours.

supply first, then demand

What to measure

Active agencies and live packages per route

Search → booking conversion

Share of bookings with a customisation

Agency response time and booking acceptance

Repeat bookings and NPS for travellers and agencies

Time from trip start to agency payout

Risks & how to handle them

Agencies take customers offline

Payment protection, reviews only for platform bookings, and tools agencies don’t want to lose

Fraud or poor-quality agencies

Verification (GST, Ministry of Tourism recognition, KYC), payment held until the trip starts, ratings

Big OTAs copy the idea

Focus on small local agencies and live customisation — a long tail big players don’t serve

Low tech comfort among agents

Assisted onboarding, a mobile workspace, WhatsApp-simple flows

12

What I learned.

Chapter 12 · looking back

Learnings

Two-sided products need two sets of empathy — every traveller feature needed an agency counterpart (live estimates only work because agencies set upgrade prices).

A shared design system saved the most time once the third product (agency workspace) arrived.

Small details — Title Case, fixed navigation, logos instead of initials — changed how trustworthy the product felt.

Next steps

Run the usability tests in section 10 and update the designs with findings.

Interview agencies on commission levels and onboarding.

Design the remaining agency screens: group departures, messages, reviews and settings.

Explore an AI trip planner and price alerts.

Sources

• WTTC Economic Impact data, reported by TravTalk India — India’s travel sector ₹21 tn (2024), ₹22 tn forecast 2025; domestic ₹16.8 tn

• Phocuswright, India Travel Market Essentials — $41.7 bn market in 2025, 57% online penetration, $47.2 bn forecast 2026 (via Travel Extra)

• Ken Research — 2.95 bn domestic tourist visits in 2024

• TTG Asia — 3–5 lakh travel agents estimated; about 14,221 registered with the Ministry of Tourism or trade groups

• Business Today (2016) — 80–85% of the holiday market serviced by individual agents; TravelTriangle quotes in 4–24 h, commission up to 10%

• Bain & Company × Google India, “How Does India Travel” — >86% online influence in research; ~40% offline bookings; distrust in payments

• Skift Research — MakeMyTrip ~54% share of India’s online travel market

• Preqin; PhocusWire — TravelTriangle marketplace with 650+ agents, commission from agents

• Company figures reported by The Quint / ThePrint — Thrillophilia 10,000+ packages, 4,500 local partners

• Dealroom — Pickyourtrail DIY customisable holiday platform
